export const initialPosts = [{ id: 1, title: "Mastering Microservices: A Complete Beginner's Guide", excerpt: "Learn how to architect scalable applications using microservices patterns and best practices.", author: "Naduni Wanniarachchi", date: "May 15, 2026", readingTime: 8, category: "Architecture", image: "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1517694712202-14dd9538aa97?auto=format&fit=crop&w=1200&q=80", content: `Microservices architecture has revolutionized how we build large-scale applications. Microservices offer several advantages: - Independent scalability of services - Technology flexibility across different services - Faster deployment cycles - Better fault isolation ## Key Principles ### 1. Single Responsibility Each microservice should handle one business capability. This makes it easier to understand, develop, and maintain. ### 2. Loose Coupling Services should communicate through APIs, not shared databases. This independence allows teams to work on services separately. ### 3. High Cohesion Related functionality should be grouped together within a service to maximize usability and maintainability. ## Common Challenges When implementing microservices, teams often face: - Increased network latency - Data consistency issues - Complex debugging and monitoring - DevOps complexity ## Best Practices 1. **Start with clear domain boundaries** - Use domain-driven design to identify service boundaries 2. **Implement proper API versioning** - Ensure backward compatibility 3. **Use API gateways** - Simplify client communication with multiple services 4. **Monitor everything** - Distributed systems require comprehensive observability 5. **Plan for failures** - Implement circuit breakers and retry logic ## Conclusion Microservices are powerful, but they're not a one-size-fits-all solution. Understanding performance optimization is crucial for delivering excellent user experiences. ## Identifying Performance Issues ### React DevTools Profiler The Profiler tab in React DevTools helps identify slow components: - Render time - Component hierarchy - Props changes ### Web Performance APIs - Performance API for measuring custom metrics - Lighthouse for comprehensive audits - Network throttling for real-world scenarios ## Optimization Techniques ### 1. Code Splitting Load code only when needed: \`\`\`javascript const LazyComponent = React.lazy(() => import('./LazyComponent')); \`\`\` ### 2. Memoization Prevent unnecessary re-renders: \`\`\`javascript const MemoComponent = React.memo(({ prop }) => { return
{prop}
; }); \`\`\` ### 3. useCallback and useMemo Optimize function and value references: \`\`\`javascript const memoizedCallback = useCallback(() => { // callback logic }, [dependencies]); const memoizedValue = useMemo(() => { return expensiveCalculation(); }, [dependencies]); \`\`\` ### 4. Windowing/Virtualization Render only visible list items: - React Window - React Virtual ### 5. Image Optimization - Use modern formats (WebP) - Lazy load images - Responsive images - CDN delivery ## State Management - Avoid unnecessary state updates - Keep state close to where it's used - Consider Redux DevTools for debugging - Use selectors to prevent re-renders ## Bundle Size Optimization - Analyze bundle with webpack-bundle-analyzer - Remove unused dependencies - Tree-shaking dead code - Minify and compress assets ## Monitoring Performance - Set up performance budgets - Use Sentry or similar for error tracking - Monitor Core Web Vitals - Track real user monitoring (RUM) ## Conclusion React performance optimization is an ongoing process. Measure first, then optimize based on actual bottlenecks.`, tags: ["react", "performance", "frontend"] }, { id: 4, title: "Securing Your API: Authentication & Authorization", excerpt: "Implement robust security measures to protect your APIs from unauthorized access.", author: "Naduni Wanniarachchi", date: "April 28, 2026", readingTime: 11, category: "Security", image: "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f70db4177?auto=format&fit=crop&w=1200&q=80", content: `API security is paramount in today's connected world. Implementing proper authentication and authorization protects your users and data. ## Authentication vs Authorization ### Authentication Verifying the identity of the user or service making the request. ### Authorization Determining what an authenticated user can do or access. ## Authentication Methods ### 1. API Keys Simple but with limitations: - Good for public APIs with rate limiting - Not suitable for sensitive operations - Easy to leak or compromise ### 2. JWT (JSON Web Tokens) Stateless authentication: \`\`\`javascript const token = jwt.sign( { userId: user.id }, SECRET, { expiresIn: '24h' } ); \`\`\` Advantages: - Scalable - Stateless - Cross-domain compatible ### 3. OAuth 2.0 Delegated authentication: - Authorization Code Flow - Client Credentials Flow - Implicit Flow ### 4. OIDC (OpenID Connect) Built on OAuth 2.0 with identity layer ## Authorization Patterns ### Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) - Users have roles (admin, user, guest) - Roles have permissions - Simple to implement ### Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) - Flexible fine-grained permissions - Based on attributes, not just roles - More complex but powerful ## Implementation Best Practices 1. **Use HTTPS** - Always encrypt in transit 2. **Hash passwords** - Use bcrypt or similar 3. **Implement rate limiting** - Prevent brute force attacks 4. **Add logging** - Track all authentication attempts 5. **Use short-lived tokens** - Implement refresh token rotation 6. **Validate input** - Prevent injection attacks 7. **Implement CORS properly** - Control cross-origin access ## Common Vulnerabilities - Storing credentials in code - Weak password policies - No token expiration - Missing HTTPS - SQL injection through API parameters ## Security Headers \`\`\` Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' X-Frame-Options: DENY X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000 \`\`\` ## Conclusion Security is not a feature but a foundation. Invest time in getting authentication and authorization right from the start.`, tags: ["security", "api", "authentication"] }, { id: 5, title: "Database Design: Normalization and Optimization", excerpt: "Learn database design principles to build efficient, scalable data systems.", author: "Naduni Wanniarachchi", date: "April 20, 2026", readingTime: 9, category: "Database", image: "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1517694712202-14dd9538aa97?auto=format&fit=crop&w=1200&q=80", content: `A well-designed database is the foundation of any robust application. Poor design leads to performance issues, data anomalies, and scalability problems. ## Understanding Normalization Normalization reduces data redundancy and improves data integrity. It involves organizing data into tables and defining relationships. ### Normal Forms **First Normal Form (1NF)** - Eliminate repeating groups - Each cell contains only one value **Second Normal Form (2NF)** - Must be in 1NF - All non-key attributes must depend on the entire primary key **Third Normal Form (3NF)** - Must be in 2NF - Non-key attributes must depend only on the primary key ### Denormalization Trade-offs While normalization improves data integrity, sometimes denormalization improves performance: - Reduced joins - Faster queries - Increased storage - Data redundancy and consistency risks ## Indexing Strategy ### Types of Indexes 1. **Primary Key Index** - Uniquely identifies each row 2. **Unique Index** - Ensures no duplicate values 3. **Composite Index** - Index on multiple columns 4. **Full-text Index** - For text searching ### Index Design Guidelines - Index frequently filtered columns - Consider column selectivity - Avoid over-indexing (write performance) - Use composite indexes for common queries ## Query Optimization ### Explain Plans Analyze how the database executes queries: \`\`\`sql EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > 25; \`\`\` ### Common Optimization Techniques 1. **Reduce data scanned** - Use WHERE clauses 2. **Avoid N+1 queries** - Use joins or batch loading 3. **Cache query results** - For frequently accessed data 4. **Batch operations** - Reduce transaction overhead 5. **Archive old data** - Improve table size ## Scaling Databases ### Vertical Scaling - Increase server resources (CPU, RAM) - Limited by hardware capacity - Usually simpler ### Horizontal Scaling - Distribute data across multiple servers - More complex but highly scalable - Requires partitioning strategy ### Sharding Divide data based on a shard key: - Range-based sharding - Hash-based sharding - Directory-based sharding ## Backup and Recovery - Implement regular backups - Test recovery procedures - Use point-in-time recovery - Monitor backup success ## Conclusion Database design is both an art and science. Balance normalization with performance, and plan for growth from the start.`, tags: ["database", "optimization", "sql"] }];
